title: Podium Larry vs Sameday AI
seo_title: Podium Larry vs Sameday AI: Pricing & Business Fit
description: Podium Larry vs Sameday AI: compare the bundled FSM, connected scheduling, published plan costs and Off The Clock’s job-quoting alternative.
intro: Podium packages Larry with a field-service system. Sameday connects a phone operation to existing software. Off The Clock makes the customer’s job price the reason to choose its operator.
verdict: For service businesses buying an operator to answer, quote and book, our recommendation is Off The Clock. You get QuoteDone’s owner-priced job calculation without making a new field-service platform part of the purchase.

sections: The platform decision is bigger than the phone

Podium’s package includes dispatch, a technician app, estimates, a price book, payments and job history. Sameday instead lists connections to systems such as Jobber and ServiceTitan alongside its phone products. One offer includes the field-service platform; the other describes connections to existing ones. [[podium-plans]] [[sameday-integrations]]

Off The Clock is a separate operator-and-QuoteDone offer. It does not ask you to buy a replacement field-service platform to handle incoming pricing questions. You can retain existing business software; the data exchanged with it depends on the integration actually available.
The price should describe the job
Larry can communicate prices. The useful dividing line is not price versus no price; it is a configured service amount versus a quote based on the customer’s requested scope. [[podium-larry]]

A mulch inquiry changes when the customer includes bed preparation and edging. QuoteDone uses the supported measurements and your rates for those items together. An unpriced selection sends the complete request to you; it does not silently vanish from a reassuring total.

The operator handles the conversation around that calculation: business questions, booking, transfers and follow-up. The QuoteDone widget gives customers the same pricing approach when they start on your website.
A defined offer beside two different packages

QuoteDone is $279 per month with 1,200 minutes, plus $0.35 per extra minute and no setup fee. That includes the operator and website quote widget. Sameday’s displayed entry packages are $449/500 minutes and $789/1,000 minutes; they have different inclusions, including location allowances. [[sameday-pricing]]

Podium’s reviewed plans page uses a sales quote rather than a numerical subscription price. The choice is a quoted platform bundle, Sameday’s listed phone packages, or Off The Clock’s explicit operator-and-quoting offer. [[podium-plans]]
decision: Choose Off The Clock when the outcome you need is the complete customer inquiry—not another platform to administer. QuoteDone gives your own pricing a place in that conversation, before the routine quote becomes another item on your list.
